key_impacts: Large quantities of radioactive material were released into the environment.
Over three hundred thousand residents were evacuated from the vicinity of the plant.
Large stretches of land were rendered uninhabitable.
Tsunami inundation caused failure of emergency power and a station blackout.
Cleanup will take decades and may cost hundreds of billions of dollars.
evidence_snippets: March 2011 accident at Japan’s Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station; large quantities of radioactivity released; residents evacuated; cleanup will take decades.
On March 11, 2011, a magnitude 9.0 earthquake set a powerful tsunami in motion.
About forty-five minutes later, the station was inundated by tsunami waves; emergency diesel generators failed, causing a station blackout.
missing_information: Specific evacuated municipalities not named; exact contamination area not quantified.
